articles.title: Wallabies fight out draw with Argentina to clinch series as Les Kiss remains unbeaten
articles.summary: Argentina 28-28 Australia in Mendoza. Wallabies rue missed opportunity but claim historic first series win in Argentina. Australia’s bright start under new coach Les Kiss is becoming a golden run after the Wallabies secured a tenacious 28-28 draw with Argentina in Mendoza to clinch their first…
body: However, the Wallabies will rue this result, squandering a two-try advantage early and a two-man advantage late that should’ve secured their first five-Test winning streak since 2021. This draw continues a historic deadlock between these rugby nations, with their last six Tests producing different winners, and squared series since 1987.

Last week Australia climbed over Argentina in the world rankings with their 27-21 victory in Jujuy. But this brave draw, played in swirling winds, was a tougher Test. Returning Wallabies winger Filipo Daugunu dropped the kickoff and it set the tone for a torrid, error-riddled arm wrestle of a first quarter in which neither team drew blood.

The Wallabies finally found their mojo, a volley of passes down the right blind side resulting in a try. Although the score was later disallowed when Ryan Lonergan was found to have fractionally crossed into touch, five minutes later they got it right. Again it was captain Harry Wilson driving over to secure a 7-0 lead after 30 minutes.

articles.title: Katie Taylor bows out from boxing as undisputed champion after dominating Flora Pili
articles.summary: Irish fans dazzled by showcase of skills in huge points win. Scorecards read 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91 in her favour. Katie Taylor signed off her storied career in style by outclassing Flora Pili on points as an 80,000 crowd at Croke Park celebrated her fairytale farewell.
body: With the gaze of Ireland upon her, the country’s great became a three-time undisputed world champion by overwhelming the previously unbeaten Frenchwoman 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 on the scorecards.
Taylor dominated through her hand speed and movement and never looked in danger as she added the vacant WBC title to her WBO, WBA and IBF belts to begin the party at GAA headquarters.
As the final seconds before retirement approached, the Olympic gold medallist ended the 10th round by trading with Pili against the ropes knowing victory was assured.
The victory completed a remarkable journey for Taylor, who began boxing at a time when girls were barred from amateur competition in Ireland and sometimes entered bouts simply as “K Taylor”.

articles.title: 'One of the best' - boxing world reacts to Taylor's farewell win
articles.summary: Some of the biggest names in women's boxing pay tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park.
body: Unified lightweight champion Caroline Dubois called Taylor "one of the best to ever do it", while Claressa Shields said the 40-year-old deserved to "ride off into the sunset".

Taylor beat Pili on points in Dublin to become undisputed light-welterweight champion and retires with 26 wins from 27 professional contests, Olympic gold and three undisputed title triumphs across two divisions.
"Thank you so much for paving the way," Londoner Dubois wrote on X. "Wishing you happiness, success and joy for this next season."
Taylor was sharper throughout, repeatedly beating the Frenchwoman to the punch before finishing with one final burst of combinations as the crowd rose to its feet.

articles.title: Francisco Cerundolo roars back from brink to stun home hope Taylor Fritz at US Open
articles.summary: Argentinian beats No 9 seed 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4. Fritz had three break points for chance to serve for match. As his last, desperate backhand soared far past the baseline inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, Taylor Fritz instantly held his face in his hands, unable to hide the agony of squandering such a…
body: For much of his afternoon, Fritz was cruising. He had established two sets to love lead against Francisco Cerundolo before breaking serve in the opening game of the third. One unfocused service game was enough to shift the momentum and once Fritz had lost control, he spent another two hours failing to retrieve it. His US Open ended with an excruciating 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4 third-round defeat by a courageous Cerundolo.

Any early loss at a home grand slam is incredibly difficult to accept, but Fritz’s timing was fatal. Having been ranked as high as No 4 last year, he is the most successful American male player of his generation. In 2024, Fritz became the first American man to reach the US Open singles final since Andy Roddick in 2006, a breakthrough run sandwiched between two quarter-final losses to Novak Djokovic in 2023 and 2025. The 28-year-old is a tremendously committed and diligent competitor who, despite his own athletic shortcomings, has eked so much out of his game. There has always been a far superior tennis player, usually an all-time great, standing before him and the major titles.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
articles.summary: Celtic come from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren. Rangers beat Motherwell 1-0 but lose Shankland to injury. Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1.
body: Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.

The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.

O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip to St Johnstone and two games against Rangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.

“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”

articles.title: Fritz and Cobolli shocked as men's seeds tumble
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz and Flavio Cobolli lose in the third round as six top-10 seeds are knocked out of the men's singles in the first week at the US Open.
body: Taylor Fritz was unable to explain how he let a two-set lead slip against Francisco Cerundolo as he became one of six top-10 seeds to be eliminated from the men's draw in the first week of the US Open.
The American ninth seed was in complete control and went an early break up in the third set, only for Argentina's Cerundolo to produce a shock 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 win to reach the fourth round.
Less than an hour later, fifth seed Flavio Cobolli of Italy fell to a 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 0-6 3-6 defeat by Belgium's Alexander Blockx, opening up the men's draw even further.
"I don't even know what to say," Fritz said. "I don't really want to talk to anybody, see anybody.

articles.title: Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph
articles.summary: Katie Taylor ends illustrious career as a three-time undisputed world champion as Croke Park gave one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures the grandest of farewells.
body: The 40-year-old outclassed unbeaten Flora Pili on points in front of 80,000 jubilant fans to add the vacant WBC belt to her WBA, WBO and IBF light-welterweight titles.

With the footwork, speed and sharp pressure fighting that defined her career, Taylor produced one final stylish performance against the overmatched Frenchwoman to win by scores of 100-90, 100-90 and 98-91.

Promoter Eddie Hearn paid tribute to Taylor, calling her "Ireland's greatest sportsperson", before she took one final lap of the ring, waving to the crowd before ceremonially placing her gloves and belts in the centre of the canvas.

After almost a quarter of a century in the sport, Taylor - an Olympic champion, two-weight world champion and one of the pioneers of women's professional boxing - finally got her fairytale ending at her dream venue.

articles.title: How Man Utd plan to compete at top with richer rivals
articles.summary: Manager Michael Carrick and chief executive Omar Berrada are united in their viewthat Manchester United can be successful despite the club's relatively low summer spending.
body: Manchester United believe they can challenge for major honours despite being unable to match the spending power of their rivals.
United spent £148m on new players this summer, less than newly promoted Ipswich, the £300m-plus invested by Chelsea and Tottenham and the record £458m spent by Manchester City.
In their victory at Ipswich on Friday night, Liverpool fielded three players, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who each cost more than £100m.

By contrast, United's most expensive signing this summer was Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a deal that could reach £70m, still £19m short of the club-record £89m they paid for Paul Pogba a decade ago.

articles.title: Mikal Bridges Reflects On Knicks’ Title Run And Comeback Wins During Playoffs
articles.summary: It’s been roughly three months since the New York Knicks became champions of the basketball world. For the first time in 53 years, and after long stretches of misery, the franchise finally reached the pinnacle of success, but the journey was not easy.
body: In fact, throughout the playoffs, the Knicks found themselves down big on several occasions, only to mount amazing comebacks that defined their run. Recently, Knicks swingman Mikal Bridges spoke about the comebacks and the conditions that made it possible to survive overwhelming odds.

The Knicks went 53-29 in the 2025-26 season, and most critics had them a tier below the Cavaliers, Celtics, and Pistons in the East. In the playoffs, however, the Knicks dominated the field, going 16-3 in an impressive performance. Along the way, they faced fierce resistance, overcoming a 22-point deficit in the opening game against the Cavaliers.

Their unlikeliest win, however, was in the Finals. In Game 4 of the series, the Knicks went down by as much as 29 points, but somehow came back and won (107-106) off a buzzer-beater from OG Anunoby. It seemed impossible at the time, but the Knicks always felt that victory was within reach.

articles.title: Gauff progresses at US Open, compatriots Fritz, Anisimova, Keys knocked out
articles.summary: Coco Gauff ensured the watching American public had something to cheer at the US Open as she progressed to the fourth round on a day when Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys suffered shock defeats.
body: Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.
The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic or the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot.
"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

body: All in all, it was a great day of football in the Bluegrass to kick off what hopes to be a fun era under Coach Stein.

“I will pick at Bama later. I’m going to go have a cold beer and f$%&#@g…excuse my French…I was going to say f-ing hang out with my family, sorry. Apologies, sorry, Big Blue Nation. They probably liked that,“ Stein quipped.

articles.title: Villa take first point but rue missed chances in Hull stalemate
articles.summary: Aston Villa picked up their first Premier League point of the season, but were left to rue missed chances in their 0-0 draw against Hull City.
body: After an improved performance against Arsenal, Unai Emery was hoping for better fortunes in what was his 200th game in charge of the Villans.

A positive start saw Nicolas Jackson head wide in the opening couple of minutes, before youngster George Hemmings managed the club's first shot on target of the season in the first quarter of an hour.

However, the reigning Europa League champions often lacked the imagination to concern the newly promoted Tigers, who looked the most threatening during the first 45 with their collection of long-range efforts.
That was until the start of the second half, which saw Villa spurn two glorious opportunities.
